# Rule reference

Every rule that `qk check` runs. Rule IDs are stable and never reused.

A rule's mode decides what a failure does: `enforced` blocks, `advisory` warns, `off` skips the rule. The `maturity` in `quality.yaml` sets the default mode. Override it per check under `modes`, using the check key. Without a `quality.yaml`, every rule is advisory.

## QK001 — quality.yaml is valid

- Check key: `manifest.valid`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: bronze, silver, gold

**What it checks.** `quality.yaml` matches the manifest schema, so every other check reads what the repo meant. An unknown key or a mistyped mode would otherwise be ignored or misread. A key under `modes` that names no known check is reported as a warning, not a failure, so a manifest written for a newer `qk` does not block an older one.

**How to fix.** Correct the key or value named in the finding. Every allowed key and value is listed in `docs/reference/manifest.md`.

## QK010 — Docs change with the code they describe

- Check key: `docs.impact`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: silver, gold

**What it checks.** When a changed file matches `paths` in an `impact_map` entry, at least one file matching that entry's `docs` must change on the same branch. A change that truly needs no docs can carry a note written by `qk docs-impact none`. The note counts only while it is part of the change and matches a person's approval in `.quality/exceptions-log.jsonl`, so a hand-written or later-edited note does not count.

**How to fix.** Update the mapped docs. If this change needs none, ask a person to approve `qk docs-impact none --reason <why> --approved-by <person>`.

## QK020 — Generated files equal their generator's output

- Check key: `generated.current`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: silver, gold

**What it checks.** Reference material is generated from code, never written by hand. For each entry under `generated` in `quality.yaml`, QK020 runs `cmd` from the repository root and compares `file` with what it wrote, ignoring line endings. A command shared by several entries runs once. Afterwards the files under `generated` are put back as they were, uncommitted changes included. Any other file that changed while the command ran is left as it is, with a warning naming it: qk cannot tell the command's changes from a person's. What such a file held before, if git did not have it, is kept as a git blob the warning names. Ignored files are not restored. Generators are slow, so QK020 runs only with `qk check --full` or when the `CI` environment variable is `true`; otherwise it is skipped. A generator that fails is a finding with its output. One that is not installed is left out; if nothing else fails, the check is skipped and names it.

**How to fix.** Run the command named in the finding and commit what it writes. Never edit a generated file by hand. For a warning about a file outside `generated`: if the command writes it, list it under `generated`.

## QK030 — No breaking OpenAPI changes

- Check key: `contracts.breaking`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: silver, gold

**What it checks.** A breaking API change should be caught before it merges, not by the clients it breaks. For each changed file matching `contracts.openapi` in `quality.yaml`, QK030 runs `oasdiff breaking` on its version at the base and its version now. Each change that breaks clients is a finding. A change oasdiff cannot confirm as breaking, such as a removed request parameter, is a warning marked `possibly breaking`. A deleted contract fails. A new one passes. A renamed one is compared with what it held under its old name. Only the listed file starts a comparison: a change in a file it reaches through `$ref` is seen when the listed file changes too. When `oasdiff` is not installed, or cannot read a contract, the check is skipped and says why.

**How to fix.** Keep the API compatible: put back what was removed, or make the new requirement optional. If the break is intended, release it as a new API version, or ask a person to approve a waiver with `qk waiver add QK030`.

## QK040 — A new spec has a threat model

- Check key: `security.threat-model`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: gold

**What it checks.** Security thinking starts when a feature is specified, not after it ships. Each Markdown file added under `security.specs_dir` in `quality.yaml` needs a threat model under `security.threat_models`, which is `docs/security/threat-models` unless you name another folder. A threat model belongs to a spec when it has the same file name, or when its frontmatter has `spec:` with the spec's path from the repository root. Only new specs are checked: editing or moving a spec needs nothing. Without a `quality.yaml`, QK040 checks `docs/specs` if that folder exists. With a `quality.yaml` that names no `specs_dir`, it checks nothing.

**How to fix.** Write a threat model for the spec and save it under `security.threat_models`, with the spec's file name or with `spec: <path of the spec>` in its frontmatter. If the spec needs none, ask a person to approve a waiver with `qk waiver add QK040`.

## QK060 — New and upgraded dependencies exist, are old enough, maintained and licensed

- Check key: `supply-chain.dependencies`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: silver, gold

**What it checks.** A release that is a day old has been read by nobody. It may be a hijacked version of a package you have trusted for years, or a name an agent invented and an attacker registered. QK060 looks at every dependency a change adds or moves to another version, in `package.json`, `go.mod`, `composer.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `Pipfile` and `requirements*.txt`. The version is the one the lockfile holds (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `composer.lock`, `Cargo.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`), so an upgrade that only changes the lockfile is found too. Without a lockfile, or for a name the lockfile does not hold, it is the version the manifest names when it names one exactly. For a range such as `^1.2.0` it is the newest release, because that is what an install without a lockfile may fetch. Each finding names the version. QK060 asks the public registry (npm, the Go module proxy, Packagist, crates.io, PyPI) four things. The package exists. That version was published at least 14 days ago. It is not deprecated, abandoned or yanked. Its licence is one of MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, 0BSD and Unlicense; for a choice of licences one of them is enough. Only what a manifest names is checked, not the dependencies of dependencies. Indirect Go requirements, paths, git URLs, workspace members and folders named `node_modules` or `vendor` are left out. The Go module proxy holds no licences, so for Go the licence is not checked. Only public registries are asked: a package from a private registry is reported as missing. QK060 uses the network, so it runs only with `qk check --full` or when the `CI` environment variable is `true`; otherwise it is skipped and names what it did not check. Answers are kept for 24 hours. A registry that cannot be reached is never a finding: the check is skipped and says which package it could not ask about.

**How to fix.** For a package that does not exist: check the name, it may be invented or misspelt. For a version that is too young: wait, or stay on an older version. For a deprecated one or a licence that is not allowed: pick another package. If a person decides the dependency is right all the same, such as an urgent security patch or a package of your own in a private registry, ask them to approve a waiver for that package alone, with `qk waiver add QK060 --package <name>@<version>`.

## QK061 — Dependencies have a lockfile that changes with them

- Check key: `supply-chain.lockfile`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: silver, gold

**What it checks.** Without a lockfile, a build installs whatever versions are newest that day, not the ones that were reviewed and tested. QK061 reads every dependency manifest git tracks or would add: `package.json` (npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun), `go.mod`, `composer.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `Pipfile`, and `pyproject.toml` when Poetry or uv is in use. A manifest that declares dependencies needs its lockfile in git. In a workspace, a lockfile in a parent folder counts. When a manifest's dependencies change, its lockfile must change in the same change set. Other edits to a manifest, such as a script or a version number, need nothing. QK061 only reads files; it never runs a package manager. Folders named `node_modules` or `vendor` are left out. Python with only `requirements.txt`, or a `pyproject.toml` without Poetry or uv, has no lockfile to check, so the check is skipped and says so. When there is no base to compare with, QK061 only checks that each lockfile is there. Outside a git repository it checks nothing.

**How to fix.** Run the package manager so it writes the lockfile (`npm install`, `pnpm install`, `yarn install`, `go mod tidy`, `composer update --lock`, `cargo generate-lockfile`, `poetry lock`, `uv lock`, `pipenv lock`), and commit the lockfile with the manifest. If the lockfile exists but is reported as missing, git ignores it: take it out of `.gitignore`. If a manifest should have no lockfile, ask a person to approve a waiver with `qk waiver add QK061`.

## QK100 — Waivers are valid, owned and not expired

- Check key: `waivers.valid`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: silver, gold

**What it checks.** A waiver in `.quality/waivers.yaml` needs a reason, an owner and an end date, so an exception cannot quietly become permanent. It also needs a matching approval in `.quality/exceptions-log.jsonl`, written by `qk waiver add`, so a hand-written or later-edited waiver does not count. An expired, incomplete or unapproved waiver never applies: the finding it covered is reported again. A waiver naming a rule this `qk` does not have is a warning, not a failure, because it hides nothing and may come from a newer `qk`. QK100 itself cannot be waived.

**How to fix.** Fix the finding and delete the waiver, or correct the field named here. To extend or change a waiver, have a person approve it again with `qk waiver add`.

## QK110 — Every top-level path has a code owner

- Check key: `ownership.codeowners`
- Phase: 1
- Enforced by default at: gold

**What it checks.** Every finding needs someone to act on it, and every change someone to review it. QK110 checks that each file and folder at the top of the repository has an owner in `CODEOWNERS`. It reads the file where the host of the `origin` remote reads it. GitHub: `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS`, then `docs/CODEOWNERS`. GitLab: `CODEOWNERS`, `docs/CODEOWNERS`, then `.gitlab/CODEOWNERS`. The first one found counts. Patterns are matched as the host matches them, and the last matching line wins, so a later line without owners takes ownership away. A top-level file has an owner when it has one itself; a top-level folder has one when a new file in it would get one. On another host, or without an `origin` remote, the check is skipped and says so. With `--changed`, only top-level paths the change adds are checked, unless the change touches `CODEOWNERS`.

**How to fix.** Add a line for the path to `CODEOWNERS`, such as `/docs/ @your-team`, or give everything a default owner with `* @your-team` on the first line. If a line without owners comes later in the file, give it an owner or remove it. If a path should have no owner, ask a person to approve a waiver with `qk waiver add QK110`.
